term: actual concrete ground; ground-ancestor of a thinker
definition: Over the #505/#510 Profile (a Kant Ontic signature, a supplied world-independent concreteness predicate and a world-local relation grounds w y x, read 'y grounds x at w'), ActualConcreteGround m w y x means that y is concrete, exists at w and grounds x at w; an abstract, non-concrete or absent ground is not counted. GroundAncestor m w x b is Mathlib's Relation.ReflTransGen of that relation: x = b, or a finite chain of actual concrete grounds leads from x to b. A thinker is a bearer of an occurring thought (DEF-THOUGHT-BEARER); nothing makes it a substance, self or person. A contingent root among a thinker's ground-ancestors is an ancestor that is contingent at w (exists at w and is absent at some accessible world) and has no actual concrete ground: a root of this relation only, not shown absolutely unexplained, temporally first, or uncaused in the efficient sense. ThinkerGroundingAccessible requires Acc (ActualConcreteGround m w) at each bearer of an occurring thought: every descending chain of actual concrete grounds from it is finite in the inductive sense of Acc. ThinkerAncestryGrounded requires an actual concrete ground only for ground-ancestors of such a bearer that are concrete, exist at w and are contingent at w.
note: Analyst's vocabulary for #564, so that the anti-brute-root and well-foundedness premises can be restricted to the ground-ancestry of the Cogito's bearer instead of the whole candidate carrier. 'Grounds' is the Profile's own relation, not Ontic.Causes, temporal succession or Aquinas's per se causal link. A sourced account of existential grounding (#545) would replace the stipulation.
